findings.headline: In a random sample, 7 of 9 charted 99215 visits were documented below the billed level
findings.interpretation: Billed 99215 on 21.8% of visits; about 3.1% expected for this panel (risk-adjusted score 5.86). 47% of its 99215s were for patients with 0-1 chronic conditions. In the random 30-chart sample, 11 of 30 (36.7%) were documented below the billed level; the peer rate for 99215 is 0%. Draft overpayment estimate $2,655 (CI $1,778-$3,531). A certified coder should re-score the charts before any recovery.

findings.headline: In a random sample, 7 of 9 charted 99215 visits were documented below the billed level
findings.interpretation: Billed 99215 on 22.5% of visits; about 3.5% expected (risk-adjusted score 5.76). The high share holds even for healthy patients (19-21% for 0-1 conditions). In the random 30-chart sample, 12 of 30 (40%) were documented below the billed level, and many 99215 notes have moderate MDM with no minutes recorded. Draft overpayment estimate $3,034 (CI $2,094-$3,973). Needs coder confirmation.

findings.headline: Most extreme claims outlier (99215 share 34% vs 2.7% expected), but the sampled charts support the billed levels
findings.interpretation: About 29% of visits for patients with no chronic conditions are 99215s (peers: 1.9%), often for back pain, URI, rash or follow-up visits. Still, all 30 random charts supported the billed level, and only 2 of 23 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review lacked a lab or test on the claim. The claims pattern is still very unusual. Recommend a certified coder review the notes for copied-forward or inflated documentation. No overpayment is supported yet.
